See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=computational+cognitive+models+of+responsibility+and+agency+hierarchical+decision+making&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Hot and Cool Executive Functions in Middle Childhood: Evidence for a Weak but Process-Specific Relationship.\", \"abstract\": \"Background: Executive functions (EFs) are cognitive and emotional abilities that underpin goal-directed behavior, decision-making, and problem-solving. EFs can be categorized into two broad types, Hot EFs and Cool EFs, distinguished by their relation to emotional processing. Cool EFs are associated with cognitive control, while Hot EFs involve emotional regulation and decision-making in emotionally charged contexts. EFs contribute to self-regulation, including the ability to adjust behavior in response to feedback. Methods: The aim of this study is to investigate the relationship between Hot (decision-making under uncertainty) and Cool (cognitive flexibility) EFs in middle childhood. To assess these dimensions of EFs, we used two tasks, the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) and the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), completed by children (N = 90) aged 6-12 years. Results: Traditional WCST indices of cognitive flexibility were not associated with IGT performance. Using hierarchical linear regression models, the most significant overlap concerns the negative relationship between post-loss adjustment in the WCST (post-loss reaction time-plRT) and learning across the IGT (learning index-LI). Children who responded faster after negative feedback (plRT ↓) showed greater improvement in advantageous choice over the course of the task (LI ↑). Conclusions: The findings suggest that decision-making in the IGT is more closely linked to dynamic, process-based aspects of self-regulation than to static measures of cognitive flexibility. It can be concluded that the relationship between WCST and IGT during middle childhood is best described as weak, process-specific, and developmentally modulated, indicating that Cool and Hot EFs are partially distinct yet interconnected systems.\", \"doi\": \"10.3390/children13081109\", \"pmid\": \"42650447\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13510344\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"full…
